Upload a file — `.geojson`, or a shapefile as a single `.zip` or as
`.shp`/`.dbf`/`.shx` selected together — and find out whether every
geometry is valid. If it isn't, the exact reason; if you want, we'll
fix it and you can download the result.

::: {.callout-tip}
**Private by design.** Your file is processed entirely in your
browser (Python via WebAssembly) — it's never uploaded to any server,
including ours. Nothing to configure, nothing to trust: the code
never gets the chance to see your data.
:::

The code itself isn't shown here — it's a fixed, non-editable check
using Shapely/GEOS underneath; see the
[full article](/posts/geometry-validity.html) for the actual code,
editable and explained line by line.

```{.webgeods-python #geometry-diagnose-py .tool-cell}
#| package: geopandas, shapely
#| helper: read_upload
import re
import geopandas as gpd
from shapely.validation import explain_validity

# explain_validity() sometimes appends the failure coordinates in
# brackets (e.g. "Self-intersection[12.5 41.9]") — split that into its
# own "position" column instead of leaving it inside the message text.
# R's st_is_valid(reason = TRUE) never includes coordinates, so R rows
# simply have no position (see geometry-validity.qmd for why). Defined
# at the top level (not inside the `if gdf is not None` block below)
# so it's always available in the session for geometry-repair-py to
# reuse, even on a run where nothing was actually loaded.
POSITION_RE = re.compile(r"^(.*?)\[([-\d.]+)\s+([-\d.]+)\]$")

# GEOS reports one of a small, CLOSED set of validity failures --
# verified against TopologyValidationError.cpp in the GEOS source
# itself, not guessed from the handful of examples this tool's own
# gallery happens to show. explain_validity()'s raw message always
# starts with one of these exact names before any bracketed position,
# so "category" here IS that same canonical name (not a machine-
# readable id underneath it): once position is split into its own
# column, the raw message never said anything category doesn't
# already say, so a separate "reason" column would just repeat it --
# found live, reviewing this table, that the two columns were showing
# the same information twice for every single row. This tool never
# surfaces three of the eleven categories (repeated points collapse
# into "too few points" as of GEOS 3.11+; duplicate rings and unclosed
# rings weren't reproducible through any geometry this tool could
# actually receive -- both GeoJSON and Shapefile close every ring at
# the FILE FORMAT level, before geopandas ever sees it).
GEOS_CATEGORIES = [
    "Ring Self-intersection",
    "Self-intersection",
    "Hole lies outside shell",
    "Holes are nested",
    "Interior is disconnected",
    "Nested shells",
    "Duplicate Rings",
    "Too few points",
    "Invalid Coordinate",
    "Repeated Point",
    "Ring is not closed",
]

def classify_reason(message):
    for category in GEOS_CATEGORIES:
        if message.startswith(category):
            return category
    return "Other"

def diagnose(geom):
    if geom.is_valid:
        # A valid geometry has no error position, but a locator is
        # still useful — representative_point() (unlike centroid,
        # guaranteed to fall ON the geometry, not just near it) gives
        # every row a place to be found on the map, not just the
        # invalid ones.
        p = geom.representative_point()
        return True, "", f"{round(p.x, 6)} {round(p.y, 6)}"
    message = explain_validity(geom)
    m = POSITION_RE.match(message)
    reason = m.group(1).strip() if m else message
    position = f"{m.group(2)} {m.group(3)}" if m else ""
    return False, classify_reason(reason), position

def export_crs(g):
    # Reprojects `g` back to the CRS it was UPLOADED in (original_crs,
    # set below and reused as a module-level global by
    # geometry-repair-py and geometry-export-shp-py) — every
    # downloadable result goes through this, so what comes out matches
    # what went in, even though the map/diagnosis above always work in
    # WGS84 (GeoJSON and MapLibre both assume it).
    if g is None or original_crs is None or original_crs == "EPSG:4326":
        return g
    return g.to_crs(original_crs)

EMPTY_FC = {"type": "FeatureCollection", "features": []}

# No built-in fallback: if nothing is readable, gdf stays None and the
# result is an empty FeatureCollection — this cell only ever runs
# after a successful upload or "Load example", so in practice this branch means the uploaded file
# itself failed to parse, not "nothing uploaded yet".
gdf, original_crs, crs_warning, _ = read_upload()

if gdf is not None:
    if "name" not in gdf.columns:
        gdf["name"] = [f"geometry {i+1}" for i in range(len(gdf))]

    diagnosis = gdf.geometry.apply(diagnose)
    gdf["valid"] = diagnosis.apply(lambda t: t[0])
    gdf["category"] = diagnosis.apply(lambda t: t[1])
    gdf["position"] = diagnosis.apply(lambda t: t[2])

    # Every other original column from the uploaded file is kept as-is
    # (only "name" was ever guaranteed above) instead of being
    # discarded. A None in one of THOSE columns (not under our
    # control) would otherwise vanish silently once this result is
    # serialized to JSON for the browser: None becomes undefined, and
    # JSON.stringify() drops undefined-valued keys entirely.
    for col in gdf.columns:
        if col != "geometry":
            gdf[col] = gdf[col].fillna("")

{
    "features": gdf.__geo_interface__ if gdf is not None else EMPTY_FC,
    "originalCrsFeatures": export_crs(gdf).__geo_interface__ if gdf is not None else EMPTY_FC,
    "crsWarning": crs_warning
}
```

`make_valid()` rebuilds the geometry into an equivalent, valid form —
reuses exactly the data just diagnosed above, no new reading of the
file.

```{.webgeods-python #geometry-repair-py .tool-cell}
from shapely.validation import make_valid

# "category"/"position" are deliberately left as they were at diagnose
# time, not recomputed here: they explain what WAS wrong (and where),
# which stays true and useful even after the geometry is fixed — a
# fresh diagnose() on the repaired geometry would just blank them out
# for every row that got fixed, erasing the one thing this table is
# for. Only "valid" reflects the CURRENT state, and it's three-valued
# instead of a separate "fixed" column: True (was already valid,
# untouched), False (still invalid — make_valid() failing to produce
# a valid result would be a bug in Shapely itself, not expected, but
# handled rather than assumed away), or the string "fixed" (was
# invalid, make_valid() repaired it) — WebGeoDS.Table's iconColumns
# (shared/table.js) renders that third state as a green "✓ fixed",
# visibly distinct from an always-valid row's plain "✓". VALIDITY_PAINT
# above treats "fixed" the same as true (green) on the map.
was_valid = gdf["valid"].copy()

gdf["geometry"] = gdf.geometry.apply(lambda g: make_valid(g) if not g.is_valid else g)

now_valid = gdf.geometry.apply(lambda g: g.is_valid)
gdf["valid"] = [
    "fixed" if (not wv) and nv else nv
    for wv, nv in zip(was_valid, now_valid)
]

# Keep every original column, fillna("") so a None in one doesn't
# silently drop that property once this result is serialized to JSON.
for col in gdf.columns:
    if col != "geometry":
        gdf[col] = gdf[col].fillna("")

{
    "features": gdf.__geo_interface__,
    "originalCrsFeatures": export_crs(gdf).__geo_interface__
}
```

```{.webgeods-python #geometry-export-shp-py .tool-cell}
# Only run on demand (see downloadButton below), not on every
# diagnose/repair: writes the CURRENT gdf, reprojected back to the CRS
# it was uploaded in (export_crs(), defined in geometry-diagnose-py —
# gdf itself stays in WGS84, the working CRS the map/diagnosis use), as
# an actual shapefile (geopandas.to_file(), confirmed to work in this
# Pyodide build), zips the resulting .shp/.shx/.dbf/.prj/.cpg in
# memory, and returns it base64-encoded — the only way to get binary
# bytes out of a cell value and into a downloadable Blob on the JS
# side.
import base64
import io
import os
import zipfile

export_crs(gdf).to_file("/tmp/webgeods_export.shp", driver="ESRI Shapefile")

buf = io.BytesIO()
with zipfile.ZipFile(buf, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as z:
    for fname in sorted(os.listdir("/tmp")):
        if fname.startswith("webgeods_export."):
            with open(f"/tmp/{fname}", "rb") as f:
                z.writestr(fname.replace("webgeods_export", "result"), f.read())

base64.b64encode(buf.getvalue()).decode("ascii")
```

*First run loads the Python engine — expect about a minute. Instant
after that, and again each time you come back to this page.*
